To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the elastic differential cross section at 37 Mev for 209Bi is well described by the spherical global optical potential by Koning and Delaroche (2003) when a modified balance of surface and volume absorption is assumed.

the elastic scattering cross section of 209Bi at 37 MeVa is significantly larger than predicted by spherical global potentials, and the discrepancy can be resolved by adjusting the balance between surface absorption and surface and volume scattering in the potential.

the elastic and inelastic neutron scattering cross sections for {sup 209,208}Bi were measured with a high statistical precision and that the results challenge the predictions from well-established global spherical optical potentials.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the improvement of the optical model and its applications to the analysis of nuclear reaction data.
the improvement of the optical model and its application to neutron-induced reactions at energies of interest in the field of applied nuclear physics.
the study of the weak particle-nucleus coupling in neutron-induced reactions on heavy targets at medium neutron energies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the present measurements provide a stringent test of global optical-model predictions at 37 Mev.
the present data and calculations do not support the weak-coupling hypothesis.
a global optical model is not available for neutron energies above {approx}30 MeV.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the weak-coupling assumption is not adequate for describing the elastic scattering data at 37 Mev.
the data are consistent with the weak particle-core-coupling assumption but challenge the accuracy of the optical potentials.
the present results provide the best data set for {sup 209,207}Bi at 37 Mev, and that the weak coupling assumption is not adequate to account for the data.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the weak particle-core-coupling approximation can be applied to medium-energy neutron scattering from {sup 209Bi} with confidence.
the weak coupling assumption is not sufficient at 37 Mev.
the weak particle-core model provides an excellent description of the data and, hence, can be used to predict the neutron elastic scattering cross section for other nuclei.
